# Every entry point the source system exposes, transcribed once so parity is
# checkable in a clone that does not have the source system.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND NOT JUST THE FEATURE INVENTORY. Four of the console
# scripts below have no Feature Inventory row at all, so a parity check keyed on
# the inventory alone passes while four real workflows vanish. Every name here
# must either be claimed by a registry entry's `source_scripts` or be listed in
# CUT.md with a one-line reason.
#
# The first block is the [project.scripts] table, thirty-three entries.
# It was thirty until 2026-09-18, when a parity audit found dj-staging-repair,
# dj-anlz-probe and dj-relocate-db in the source system's scripts table and in
# neither this file nor CUT.md, so the contract test could not see them at all.
# All three are now cut, with reasons, in CUT.md.

dj-pipeline
dj-setid
dj-sort-inbox
dj-sort-unplaced
dj-sync
dj-audit-genres
dj-pad-camelot
dj-path-repair
dj-tag-folder

dj-resort-energy

dj-split-genre-folders
dj-genre-research

# The second block is workflows that are NOT console scripts and would therefore
# be invisible to a check that read the scripts table alone. The backup script
# ships as package data; the two restamp entry points are deliberately excluded
# from the scripts table because they are one-shot migrations, which is a reason
# not to put them on a user's PATH, not a reason for them to have no verb.

backup.sh
master_set.sh
energy_restamp
